name: Shadow
what_it_is: Shadow is a discrete-event network simulator that executes real, unmodified application code as native Linux processes by intercepting system calls and integrating them into a virtual simulated network. It is designed to scale to thousands (up to hundreds of thousands) of network-connected processes while maintaining deterministic, reproducible simulation runs.
components: system call interposition layer (over 150 syscalls implemented)
virtual network stack (private simulated network per run)
process execution engine (runs unmodified Linux binaries)
protocols: TLS (used by applications via intercepted syscalls)
HTTP (demonstrated in examples via real curl/python processes)
measurement: Per-process stdout/stderr captured in host subdirectories
configuration: Network graph specification (built-in or custom graph)
Multiple virtual hosts supported in a single config
modes: Deterministic replay — same config produces identical runs
constraints: Only runs on Linux (uses Linux syscall interposition)
Does not yet fully support all Linux syscall API features — applications relying on unsupported or complex syscall behavior may fail
Fault injection capabilities (packet loss, latency, jitter, bandwidth limits) not confirmed in fetched documentation
